Thanks,
Claire

Recap:
- Deployment modes: Hosted API (fastest to prod, multi-tenant) vs Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput, data isolation) vs Private (VPC/on-prem for regulated PHI workflows).
- Migration concerns: tokenization differences are usually minor but we plan a model verification pass + evals; fallbacks can be done by routing traffic to old provider during canary.

Questions for you (so the SE session is productive):
1) Which workloads must remain entirely in your VPC/on-prem for compliance? (list by product/endpoint)
2) Expected QPS and p95 latency SLO for the top three endpoints.
3) Do you currently use custom tokenization or fine-tuned models that need to be ported?

Proposed next steps:
- Technical deep dive (60 min) with Dev (cc'd) to confirm network, KMS, and migration plan — Thu 4/8 9:30–10:30am PST or Fri 4/9 10–11am PST.
- I will share a migration checklist and a sample canary cutover playbook before the call.
- If Private is required we can start a security scoping and provide an on-prem deployment estimate (timeline + prelim infra bill).

I'll prepare the migration playbook and a short one-pager that compares operational lift (people, week-of cutover tasks, rollback steps) for Dedicated vs Private.

Subject: Re: Follow-up: deployment options after today's demo — proposed tech agenda

Hi Claire — thanks for sending the diagram. A few tech notes to shape the call:

- Networking: For Private VPC we support customer-managed subnets, NAT, and private endpoints. We'll need the CIDR ranges and any egress restrictions to provide a connection plan.
- KMS/HSM: We integrate with common cloud KMS (AWS, GCP) and can support bring-your-own HSM for on-prem.
- Data flow & caching: For migration we recommend enabling prefix/KV caching during cutover to avoid cold-start tokenization spikes; this minimizes token cost and keeps latency stable.
- Compatibility: If you rely on a specific tokenizer or have locally fine-tuned weights, we can run a model parity eval (same prompts) and surface diffs.

Agenda for the SE call (60m):
1) Architecture walk-through (15m) — your infra/infra-app owners
2) Security & compliance checklist + SOC-2 questionnaire review (15m)
3) Migration strategy: model parity, tokenization checks, canary routing, fallback (20m)
4) Timeline + next steps & handoffs (10m)

I can run through a sample canary cutover playbook and a checklist of test prompts to validate parity. Confirming Thu 4/8 9:30am PST works for me.
